docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Generative AI Project Template

Template for a new AI Cloud project.

Click on Use this template to start your own project!

This project is a generative ai template. It contains the following features: LLMs, information extraction, chat, rag & evaluation. It uses LLMs(local or cloud), NiceGUI (frontend) & FastAPI (backend) & Promptfoo as an evaluation and redteam framework for your AI system.

Test LLM

Engineering tools:

  • [x] Use UV to manage packages in a workspace (frontend and backend).
  • [x] pre-commit hooks: use ruff to ensure the code quality & detect-secrets to scan the secrets in the code.
  • [x] Logging using loguru (with colors)
  • [x] Pytest for unit tests
  • [x] Dockerized project (Dockerfile & docker-compose).
  • [x] NiceGUI (frontend) & FastAPI (backend)
  • [x] Make commands to handle everything for you: install, run, test

AI tools:

  • [x] LLM running locally with Ollama or in the cloud with any LLM provider (LiteLLM)
  • [x] Information extraction and Question answering from documents
  • [x] Chat to test the AI system
  • [x] Efficient async code using asyncio.
  • [x] AI Evaluation framework: using Promptfoo, Ragas & more...

CI/CD & Maintenance tools:

  • [x] CI/CD pipelines: .github/workflows for GitHub (Testing the AI system, local models with Ollama and the dockerized app)
  • [x] Local CI/CD pipelines: GitHub Actions using github act
  • [x] GitHub Actions for deploying to GitHub Pages with properdocs gh-deploy
  • [x] Renovate .github/renovate.json for automatic dependency and security updates
  • [x] Issues & PRs templates

Documentation tools:

  • [x] Wiki creation and setup of documentation website using properdocs (mkdocs-material)
  • [x] GitHub Pages deployment using mkdocs gh-deploy plugin

docs.title: 1. Getting started
docs.text:
This project is a monorepo containing two main packages:

  • frontend: A NiceGUI application.
  • backend: A FastAPI application that serves the AI models and business logic.

The project uses uv as a package manager and is configured as a workspace, so dependencies for both packages can be installed with a single command.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
• frontend/: The NiceGUI frontend application.
    • pyproject.toml: Frontend-specific dependencies.
    • src/: Source code for the frontend.
  • backend/: The FastAPI backend application.
    • pyproject.toml: Backend-specific dependencies.
    • src/: Source code for the backend.
  • .github/: GitHub-specific files.
    • workflows/: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines.
    • dependabot.yml: Dependabot configuration for dependency updates.
  • assets/: Static assets like images.
  • scripts/: Utility scripts.
  • tests/: Pytest unit and integration tests.
  • .env.example: Example environment variables. Create a .env from this.
  • Dockerfile: To build the application container.
  • docker-compose.yml: To run services like frontend, backend, and ollama.
  • .gitlab-ci.yml: GitLab CI configuration file.
  • Makefile: Main entry point that includes modular makefiles.
  • makefiles/: Modular makefile includes organized by purpose.
    • common.mk: Shared variables (colors, UV path, Ollama models).
    • install.mk: Installation targets (uv, dependencies, Ollama).
    • dev.mk: Development targets (run frontend/backend, pre-commit).
    • test.mk: Testing targets (pytest, Ollama tests).
    • build.mk: Build and Docker targets.
    • ci.mk: CI/CD targets (GitHub Actions locally).
    • clean.mk: Cleanup targets (cache management).
  • pyproject.toml: Defines uv workspace and shared dependencies.
  • uv.lock: Lock file for uv package manager.
  • .pre-commit-config.yaml: Configuration for pre-commit hooks.
  • mkdocs.yml: Configuration for the documentation site.
  • README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, LICENSE: Project documentation.

docs.title: 1.1. Local Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or MacOS
  • git clone the repository
  • uv & Python 3.12–3.14.8 (uv installs a compatible interpreter)
  • Create a .env file (take a look at the .env.example file)

docs.title: 1.2 ⚙️ Steps for Installation
docs.text: This project uses a Makefile to simplify the installation and execution process.

docs.title: Local Installation
docs.text:
1. For CPU-based environment (or MacOS) To install all dependencies for both frontend and backend for a CPU environment, run:
make install-dev
  1. For NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) environment If you have an NVIDIA GPU and want to use CUDA for acceleration, run:
make install-dev-cuda

This will install the CUDA-enabled version of PyTorch.

docs.title: Using Docker
docs.text:
The project can be fully containerized using Docker. This is the recommended way to run the application as it handles all services and networks.

  • The docker-compose.yml and docker-compose-cuda.yml files define the services.
  • To run the entire application stack using Docker Compose with CPU support:
make docker-compose
  • To run with CUDA support, make sure you have a GPU and the necessary drivers installed. Follow this guide to set it up. Then run:
make docker-compose-cuda
  • To rebuild and run (useful after code changes):
# CPU
make docker-compose-rebuild
# CUDA
make docker-compose-cuda-rebuild

docs.title: Using Local vs. Cloud LLMs
docs.text:
• Local model (Ollama):
    • Install Ollama: make install-ollama
    • Ensure Ollama is running (make run-ollama can help).
    • Set your .env file to point to the local Ollama endpoint (copy and paste from the .env.example file).
    • Download a model: make download-ollama-models
    • Test the connection: make test-smoke-ollama
    • Test the connection: make test-integration-llm
  • Cloud model (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.):
    • Update your .env file with the correct API keys and model names, following the LiteLLM naming convention.
    • Test the connection: make test-integration-llm

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text:
Once installed (either locally or via Docker), you can run the services.

  • Run Everything: The make run-app command is the easiest way to start all services, including the frontend, backend, database, and Ollama.

  • Run Services Individually:

    • Run Backend: make run-backend
    • Run Frontend: make run-frontend

You can then access:

  • Frontend (NiceGUI): http://localhost:8080 (or the configured port)
  • Backend (FastAPI): http://localhost:8000 (or the configured port). Docs http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: Comprehensive software validation
docs.text: make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and CI. It includes every existing self-contained and real-service integration suite. Configure the services and dedicated test credentials in the testing guide before running it. A focused make test-local pass does not establish full validation. Missing services or skipped integration must be reported as incomplete. Coverage and artifact/runtime checks remain explicit alongside this command.

docs.title: CLAUDE.md
docs.text: Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code) in this repository.

docs.title: What this repo is
docs.text: A template for a generative AI application, managed with uv as one project with two packages: backend/ (FastAPI, genai_template_backend) and frontend/ (NiceGUI, genai_template_frontend), plus Ollama, docker-compose, tests, a documentation site (properdocs / MkDocs Material) and semantic-release. A release bumps the three versions together (root, backend/, frontend/) and publishes a GitHub release with both packages' wheels and sdists, plus the documentation on GitHub Pages; there is no package index. Developer docs: docs/developer/.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
make install-dev          # .venv with dev and docs tools (install-dev-cuda for CUDA)
make pre-commit-install   # git hooks (checks and commit message format)
make test-all           # required comprehensive software validation
make pre-commit           # static hooks; make test-all remains required
make run-app              # Ollama + backend + frontend (run-backend / run-frontend alone)
make docker-compose       # the same in containers (docker-compose-cuda for CUDA)
make build-package        # dist/ wheels + sdists of backend and frontend
make deploy-doc-local     # build and serve the documentation
make release-version      # semantic-release: versions, CHANGELOG, tag, GitHub release (main/dev, clean, in sync)
make release-assets       # attach dist/ to the GitHub release
make release              # release-version + build-package + release-assets (manual release)
make deploy-doc-gh        # documentation to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use the make targets; workflows call make, never re-implement a step. A manual release and a GitHub Actions release run the same targets (makefiles/release.mk).
  • Never commit, push, tag, create a GitHub release, run make release* / make deploy-doc-gh or gh workflow run without asking first.
  • make release-version must keep its guards: branch main or dev, clean tree, in sync with origin, token from GH_TOKEN, then gh auth login, then a prompt. Never print a credential.
  • Versions, tags and CHANGELOG.md belong to semantic-release (Conventional Commits, docs/developer/3.conventions.md): never edit a project.version by hand. The three pyproject.toml versions always stay equal.
  • Settings in backend_settings.py / frontend_settings.py; secrets as SecretStr, set by environment or .env, never in a file of the repository. A new or renamed environment variable also goes in .env.example (and .env.example.docker if the containers read it) and, if CI needs it, in the workflow env:.
  • Logging with each package's loguru logger (from genai_template_backend.backend_settings import logger, the same for the frontend).
  • Unit tests run in parallel (pytest-xdist): no shared state between tests.
  • Docs: numbered pages in docs/developer/, one purpose line, numbered steps, short tables, no long prose. Keep properdocs.yml nav and the README table in step.

docs.title: Required software validation
docs.text: make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and CI. make test-local is only a focused diagnostic command. A local-only pass, integration collection, or skipped/unavailable integration does not establish full validation. Keep coverage and artifact/runtime checks explicit alongside software validation. Never execute live authentication/integration without the user's authorization; if it was not authorized or services are unavailable, report full validation as incomplete instead of claiming the change fully verified.

docs.title: Contributing to this project
docs.text:
Thanks for taking the time to contribute! Everyone taking part follows the Code of Conduct; report unacceptable behavior by opening an issue.

Team members: the contributors of the repository.

  1. Set up once: 1. Setup (make install-dev, make pre-commit-install).
  2. Comment on (or create) the issue and wait to be assigned, then branch off dev (feature/<name>, bugfix/<name>) and follow the Conventions.
  3. Before pushing: make test-all and make pre-commit (4. Testing). CI runs the same make targets, so what passes locally passes in CI.
  4. Open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention: it decides the next version. Pull requests are squash-merged.
  5. Releases are made by semantic-release, never by hand-made tags: 5. Release.

Security issues: SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Get a working development environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Version Needed for make, bash, git Ubuntu 22.04+ or macOS defaults everything uv recent everything; make install-uv installs it Python >= 3.12 (requires-python) everything; uv downloads it Ollama any optional: a local LLM (make install-ollama) Docker + docker-compose any optional: make docker-compose NVIDIA GPU + drivers — optional: the CUDA variants gh CLI any optional: make release* from a laptop

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git
cd generative-ai-project-template
make install-dev            # backend + frontend + dev and docs tools, CPU (or: make install-dev-cuda)
make pre-commit-install     # git hooks: checks on commit, commit message format
cp .env.example .env        # LLM endpoints and keys (see .env.example)
make test-all             # required: unit/component and real LLM/Ollama/API integration

Install only one side: make install-backend (or install-backend-cuda), make install-frontend. Production dependencies only: make install-prod (or install-prod-cuda).

docs.title: Run
docs.text: Command Starts make run-backend FastAPI on http://localhost:8000 (docs: /docs) make run-frontend NiceGUI on http://localhost:8080 make run-frontend-backend both make run-app Ollama + both

docs.title: Local LLM (Ollama)
docs.text:
make install-ollama            # macOS (Homebrew) or Linux
make download-ollama-models    # OLLAMA_MODEL_NAME and OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME
make run-ollama                # serves on http://localhost:11434
make test-smoke-ollama               # one generate call
make test-integration-llm        # the LLM client against INFERENCE_* from .env

A cloud model instead: set INFERENCE_* / EMBEDDINGS_* in .env with LiteLLM model names.

docs.text: Command Runs make docker-compose backend, frontend and Ollama (CPU) make docker-compose-cuda the same with CUDA (docker-compose-cuda.yml) make docker-compose-rebuild rebuild the images first

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
A uv workspace with two packages that share one version and one git tag.

pyproject.toml          workspace root: shared dev/docs tools, ruff, pytest, semantic-release, commitizen
backend/                package genai-template-backend (FastAPI)
  pyproject.toml        backend dependencies (cpu / cuda extras for PyTorch)
  src/genai_template_backend/
    app.py              FastAPI application
    api/llm.py          LLM client (LiteLLM)
    api/routes/chat.py  chat routes
    backend_settings.py settings (pydantic-settings, .env) and the loguru logger
frontend/               package genai-template-frontend (NiceGUI)
  src/genai_template_frontend/
    main.py             NiceGUI application
    components/chat.py  chat component
    frontend_settings.py
tests/                  pytest; tests/api, tests/frontend, root-level LLM/Ollama tests
scripts/                emoji_commit_parser.py (semantic-release), docs generators
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
docs/developer/         these pages
docker-compose*.yml     backend, frontend, Ollama services
Dockerfile, Dockerfile.ollama
.github/                workflows, composite actions, Renovate, issue and PR templates

docs.title: Add a backend route
docs.text:
1. Add the route in backend/src/genai_template_backend/api/routes/ (an APIRouter).
  2. Include the router in app.py.
  3. Add a test in tests/api/. It appears in /docs automatically.

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to the right BaseEnvironmentSettings class in backend_settings.py (or frontend_settings.py). A secret is a SecretStr.
  2. Add it, with a safe example value, to .env.example.
  3. Read it through the module-level settings object.

docs.title: Add a dependency
docs.text: uv add --package genai-template-backend <pkg> (or --package genai-template-frontend), then commit uv.lock.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Python >=3.12, ruff (line length 100, Google docstrings): make format, make lint. Docstrings feed the API reference of the documentation site.
  • Use the make targets; check make help before writing a long command.
  • Settings come from backend_settings.py / frontend_settings.py (pydantic-settings, .env), never os.environ scattered in the code. Secrets are SecretStr.

  • Logging: the loguru logger from the settings module (colored, level LOGGING_LEVEL):

    from genai_template_backend.backend_settings import logger

logger.info(f"Loaded {count} documents")

  • Log the error, then raise it; skip the raise only when the loop must go on:

    except Exception as e:
    logger.error(e)
    raise

  • Prefer an if check over catching and re-raising when you can (log, then raise).

  • Large data: Polars. CPU-bound work: multiprocessing pool map. I/O: asyncio.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Comment on (or create) the issue and wait to be assigned.
  2. Branch off dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>. Stay up to date with git merge dev (branch already pushed) or git rebase dev (local only).
  3. Open a pull request to dev; its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  4. When dev is ready, a pull request dev → main releases it.
  5. After a release, merge main back into dev (merge commit, direct push). On conflicts on CHANGELOG.md or a pyproject.toml version, keep main's.
Merge Strategy Why feature/* → dev squash one conventional commit per feature dev → main squash one commit for semantic-release to evaluate main → dev (sync) merge commit, direct push [skip ci] in the release commit prevents a spurious RC

Never edit a version in pyproject.toml or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does both.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Type Release feat, feature minor fix, bugfix, hotfix, perf patch feat! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer major refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none 
✨ feat(llm): add streaming responses
🐛 fix(api): handle empty LLM response
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 chat route

Common scopes: llm, api, frontend, backend, ci, deps. The commit message is checked on commit (commitizen) and the pull request title by ci.yml.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs on commit. For a line that intentionally references a secret placeholder (${{ secrets.X }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. File-level exclusions in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the settings class, .env.example (with a safe example value), the workflow env: and a repository secret if CI needs it. Release variables are listed in 5. Release.

docs.title: Dependencies (Renovate)
docs.text:
Renovate (.github/renovate.json) opens pull requests with the renovate label, after a 7-day cooldown; security fixes are not grouped and open at once. Runtime dependencies include exact pins and ranges; uv.lock makes builds reproducible. Review every Renovate pull request; a dependency dashboard issue lists the pending ones.

  1. Keep requires-python at >=3.12,<=3.14.8 in every package manifest. Write code compatible with Python 3.12; CI runs make test-all on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.
  2. Renovate widens the Python upper bound while preserving the 3.12 minimum. Python Docker updates share the runtime update group; review the resulting supported range before merging.
  3. PyPI updates use strict Python compatibility filtering. Weekly lockfile maintenance refreshes versions already permitted by dependency ranges; review the lockfile and CI results too.
  4. Renovate updates dependency files, GitHub Actions and pre-commit revisions; update README and developer documentation when the supported Python range changes. Docs are not rewritten automatically.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text:
make test-all is the required comprehensive software check for users, developers and GitHub Actions. Run it before reporting that the software is fully validated. It runs the self-contained suites first, then real-service integration tests where a suite exists. make test-local remains a focused diagnostic shortcut; passing it does not establish full validation. The ambiguous make test target is removed.

Keep static quality, coverage reporting and artifact/runtime checks explicit alongside software tests. make check combines static checks, make test-all and strict documentation validation. It can call real services. make help lists focused commands and their requirements.

The comprehensive command does not accept per-suite ARGS filters; use focused targets for selected tests. Worker-count options remain available.

docs.title: Required checks
docs.text:
1. Run make install-dev.
  2. Start Ollama, install the selected model and configure INFERENCE_BASE_URL, INFERENCE_API_KEY and INFERENCE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME for that real service.
  3. Run make test-all, make pre-commit and make docs-build.
  4. Run artifact/runtime checks and make test-hardware-cuda separately when applicable.

make test-all runs unit tests and NiceGUI component/page simulations, then real LLM, Ollama and API-to-LLM integration tests serially. Endpoint probes run inside fixtures, never at collection. Plain uv run pytest and make test-local exclude integration/hardware execution; neither is the required comprehensive check. Self-contained tests and collection use synthetic fallback settings.

Focused command Scope make test-unit Settings and isolated logic, parallel make test-component NiceGUI simulations without a browser or real backend make test-local Unit/component tests only; insufficient for full validation make test-integration-check Credential-free collection; no endpoint probes make test-integration-llm Real inference client tests make test-integration-ollama Real Ollama tests, possibly downloading the selected model make test-smoke-ollama One generation request; a focused connectivity check make test-hardware-cuda Explicit CUDA hardware check

docs.title: Incomplete integration validation
docs.text:
Integration commands fail when tests fail, no tests execute, or any integration test is skipped or deselected. Missing credentials, unavailable services and failed cleanup therefore cannot become a successful comprehensive check. Collection/compilation alone does not establish connectivity. Report the exact checks executed and list unavailable, skipped or unexecuted checks as incomplete. Never substitute a successful focused suite for the required make test-all result.

Pytest integration runs print skip reasons and write reports/integration.json and reports/integration.xml. GitHub Actions always adds the comprehensive job outcome to its summary, including when prerequisites fail before tests can start. Coverage is reported by its own command/job.

When a cloud-only endpoint is selected, Ollama tests are inapplicable and skip; the integration gate reports incomplete validation. Use a configured Ollama service for the comprehensive template check. Provider-specific commands remain useful for focused connectivity checks. Coverage instrumentation is not currently configured; UI simulation does not prove a real browser/container works.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The software test matrix covers Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 within requires-python (>=3.12). Each matrix job installs its selected interpreter and runs make test-all.

CI and both release workflows invoke make test-all. The software job installs and starts a dedicated Ollama instance on the hosted runner, stores model data under runner.temp and pulls the selected model before running tests. INTEGRATION_OLLAMA_MODEL optionally overrides the existing template default qwen3.5:0.8b. CI sets INFERENCE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434, a non-secret local Ollama API-key placeholder and INFERENCE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME=ollama/<model> explicitly; it does not copy a developer .env or require cloud credentials. The service is stopped even after failure.

An unavailable service/model or any skipped integration fails comprehensive validation and is visible in the workflow summary. Pre-commit and the existing Compose/runtime checks remain separate.

docs.title: What make pre-commit checks
docs.text:
Hook Checks pre-commit-hooks large files, TOML/YAML/JSON syntax, end of file, whitespace, merge conflicts, LF line endings, test file names ruff, ruff-format lint (docstrings, unused imports) and format detect-secrets no credential in a file markdownlint-cli2, codespell Markdown style and spelling properdocs build --strict the documentation builds, no broken link (on docs/ or properdocs.yml changes) uv-lock uv.lock matches the pyproject.toml files commitizen (on commit) commit message format

pip-audit, actionlint, zizmor, bandit and markdown-link-check are present in .pre-commit-config.yaml but commented out.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish a version to GitHub: by hand from a laptop, or by GitHub Actions after a merge. Both run the same make targets.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    hand["<b>By hand</b><br/>make release, on a laptop"]
    ci["<b>By GitHub Actions</b><br/>pull request merged into dev or main"]
    checks["Checks: pre-commit, tests"]
    ver["release-version: bump the 3 versions, CHANGELOG.md, commit, tag v<version>,<br/>push, GitHub release<br/>(on main or dev, clean tree, in sync with origin)<br/>stops here if no feat, fix or perf"]
    build["build-package: backend + frontend wheels and sdists"]
    assets["release-assets"]
    docs["deploy-doc-gh<br/>(Actions: main only; by hand: run it yourself)"]
    gh[("GitHub release<br/>wheels, sdists")]
    pages[("GitHub Pages<br/>gh-pages branch")]

    ci --> checks --> ver
    hand --> ver
    ver --> build --> assets --> docs
    assets -.-> gh
    docs -.-> pages

docs.title: What a release publishes
docs.text:
What Where By hand By GitHub Actions version in pyproject.toml, backend/pyproject.toml, frontend/pyproject.toml (bumped together), CHANGELOG.md, tag v<version>, GitHub release this repository make release-version merge to main (stable) or dev (-rc.<n>) genai_template_backend and genai_template_frontend wheels + sdists on the GitHub release GitHub releases make build-package release-assets main and dev documentation site GitHub Pages (gh-pages branch) make deploy-doc-gh main only

The version comes from the commit messages since the last tag (3. Conventions): no feat/fix/perf, no release.

Branch Releasable commit Version dev feat, fix, perf v1.1.0-rc.1 → v1.1.0-rc.2 (GitHub prerelease) dev feat! / BREAKING CHANGE v2.0.0-rc.1 main feat, fix, perf v1.1.0 (stable) + docs main feat! / BREAKING CHANGE v2.0.0 + docs

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
gh auth login                  # once
git checkout main && git pull  # a clean main in sync with origin (dev for a release candidate)
make release                   # release-version, build-package, release-assets
make deploy-doc-gh             # the documentation site, after a release on main

make deploy-doc-gh builds the site and force-pushes the gh-pages branch; it is not part of make release. Once the workflows run, release by GitHub Actions only, so each release comes from a merged pull request.

docs.title: Guards of make release-version
docs.text:
Check Refused with branch is main or dev Release from main or dev only (on <branch>) git status --porcelain is empty Uncommitted changes: commit or stash first HEAD equals origin/<branch> after git fetch <branch> is not in sync with origin/<branch> a GitHub token is available No GitHub token: set GH_TOKEN or run gh auth login a feat/fix/perf since the last tag, tag not already there nothing released (exit 0)

The release commit (chore(release): v<version> [skip ci]) is authored with your git identity (the bot's in CI) and created with git hooks disabled for that one call, so pre-commit does not rewrite CHANGELOG.md mid-release.

docs.title: Credentials on a laptop
docs.text:
Order Method Setup 1 GH_TOKEN in the shell or .env a token with the repo scope 2 gh auth login once; make reads it with gh auth token 3 hidden prompt nothing (terminal only) 
flowchart TB
    g1{"1. GH_TOKEN set?"}
    g2{"2. gh auth login done?"}
    g3{"3. running in a terminal?"}
    g4["use it"]
    g5["prompt: token (hidden)"]
    g6["stop with an error"]
    g1 -- yes --> g4
    g1 -- no --> g2
    g2 -- yes --> g4
    g2 -- no --> g3
    g3 -- yes --> g5
    g3 -- no --> g6

make release-assets calls gh, which uses steps 1 and 2. GitHub Actions passes the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN as GH_TOKEN, so step 1 always succeeds there.

docs.title: By GitHub Actions
docs.text: Workflow Trigger Does 👷 CI — Validate (ci.yml) push or pull request, except on main/dev PR title, pre-commit, tests, docker-compose smoke test 🔶 Release — Dev (dev-release.yml) push to dev (not [skip ci]) checks, make release-version, make build-package, make release-assets 🚀 Release — Main (main-release.yml) push to main (not [skip ci]) the same, then make deploy-doc-gh Renovate schedule dependency pull requests (3. Conventions)

docs.title: Repository settings (once)
docs.text:
1. Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions: "Read and write permissions".
  2. Create the gh-pages branch once with make deploy-doc-gh (a classic token from https://github.com/settings/tokens if asked for a password).
  3. Settings → Pages: "Deploy from a branch: gh-pages". If GitHub refuses to deploy from the branch, see this discussion.
  4. Pull requests: squash merge only.

docs.text: Create your repository with GitHub's "Use this template", then rename.
